origin/main.adaptation: The README numbers predated cross-references and multi-file support, so they were quietly wrong. Re-measuring rather than trusting them is what exposed the regression; the README now records both the corrected numbers and the fact that cold compilation is genuinely 6 ms slower as the honest cost of the convergence pass, which is not a regression.

summary: Found and fixed a 6x performance regression by re-measuring my own stale published numbers. The reuse lookup was quadratic: it shifted a cached block once per comparison, so a one-word edit reached 178 ms p95 against a 200 ms target despite reusing 499 of 500 blocks. Now 29.678 ms. 72 tests pass.

usage.evidence: Benchmark rerun before and after on the same 118700-byte 500-paragraph fixture: one-word edit p95 178.760 ms then 29.678 ms; cold 27.366 ms; warm unchanged 0.933 ms. cargo test 72 pass; clippy clean; fmt clean; harness 21/21; corpus 9 ok
